sentences.text: Shri Ahadulla Usmani - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Mohan Sausarkar - Govt. Advocate appearing on beha  Advocate General.

The applicant has called in question the FIR registered  580/2024 under Sections 420, 467, 468, 470, 471, 120-B IPC at  Station Umaria, District Umaria.
 Issue notice to the respondent No.6 on payment of proc seven days.
The State counsel is directed to call for the case diary.
Also heard on interim relief.
It is contended by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant has been caught in a dispute between a husband and wife.
The wife of the complainant namely Shaheen Mansoori is running a school known as Bright Star Public School while the applicant is running a school known as Bright Future School, both at Umaria.

It is contended by counsel for the applicant that some enquiry was conducted into the affairs of the school run by wife of complainant and the State authorities reached to a conclusion by some order dated 21.10.2024 that the wife of complainant is indulging in illegal practices in running of the school because the school does not have recognition or permission.

Based on the said letter of Superintendent of Police, a Writ 2 MCRC-53306-2024 Petition No. 34464/2024 was filed before this Court where this Court looking to the findings in the aforesaid letter dated 21.10.2024 issued directions to the police authorities to register FIR because sufficient grounds were made out indicating irregularities in the matter of imparting education to the students.

It is the case of the petitioner that subsequently when the FIR was lodged in terms of the said direction of this Court then the applicant was also roped in the matter who is running a different school known as Bright Future Public School.
It is contended that the only allegation against the present applicant is that he has given admission to students studying in the school of wife of complainant in his school.

The learned counsel for the applicant relies on Section 18(3) of the Right of Children to Free and Mohammad Raiesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129323828/
1 Compulsory Education Act, 2009 whereby as per first proviso the neighbouring school has to admit the children studying in the derecognized school.

entities.text: Mohammad Raiesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is contended that even if the petitioner has given admission to the children studying in the school run by wife of complainant, then it is authorized act in terms of Section 18(3) of RTE Act and the said aspect has not been considered by the authorities while registering the FIR against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for interim relief.

Considering the limited grounds on which interim relief can be granted in a petition for quashing of FIR in view of judgment of Supreme Court in the case of Neeharika Infrstructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of 3 MCRC-53306-2024 Maharashtra reported in 2021(19) SCC 401 , this Court is of the opinion that sufficient reasons are made out to grant interim relief.

entities.text: Neeharika Infrstructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of 3 MCRC-53306-2024 Maharashtra reported in 2021(19) SCC 401
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, by way of interim relief, it is directed that no coercive steps be taken against the applicant in pursuance to the FIR in question without the leave of this Court.
It is made clear that this Court has not stopped investigation into the matter and the applicant will cooperate in the investigation.
It would be open for him to apply for anticipatory bail in accordance with law.

(VIVEK JAIN) JUDGE nks Mohammad Raiesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129323828/
2
